Subject: [Dawn] Re: How should we determine the minimum public discovery information?
    
    Hi Chenguang, Two things from running discovery documents and an MCP crawler, and a short answer to your last question. Protocol. "MCP" alone was not enough for us to talk to an endpoint. Since 2026-07-28, MCP servers start a session in one of two incompatible ways. Of the 21,474 remote servers from the official MCP registry that our crawler (HISTOR) has read since 25 October, 4,097 use the new 2026-07-28 way and 17,375 still need initialize. Our own client got the fallback wrong for three days and stopped reading about 2,000 servers it had read on 28 October. So I think 8.2 should say that the protocol comes with a version, or that the binding says how to find it. Freshness. A version number does not tell a client that a description has changed. Between 24 September and 20 October, 81% of the tool definition changes we recorded (17,401 of 21,401) kept the same serverInfo.version. The optional digest on the description endpoint does tell it. That may be worth a sentence next to Freshness. Your elements fit the discovery document in draft-artamokhov-dawn-marketplace-discovery: our "name" is your Display Name, "catalogue_url" is an Endpoint for continuing discovery, "protocol_versions" are its protocols, and "generated_at" is Freshness. The signing key is a Trust Reference outside the minimum, which is how we use it too.     Aleksandr,
    
    Thanks. I agree they are complementary.
    
    Per the DAWN charter, the discovered AI resource may itself be a service such as a catalog that furthers the discovery process. So bootstrap discovery can return the minimum public information needed to reach such a catalog.
    
    I would still keep the metadata reference resource-specific, e.g., pointing to an Agent Card. Catalog search, capability comparison, ranking, or selection after reaching the catalog remain outside the bootstrap scope.
    
    Best regards,
    Linda
    
    
    From: Александр Артамохов <alexar76=40rambler.ru@dmarc.ietf.org>
    Sent: Saturday, October 31, 2026 10:51 PM
    To: adrian@olddog.co.uk; dawn@ietf.org; Linda Dunbar <linda.dunbar@futurewei.com>
    Subject: RE: [Dawn] Updated draft-dunbar-dawn-infra-assisted-discovery
    
    Hi Linda,
    
    Thank's for the update.
    
    The clear boundary in -03 is helpful: bootstrap discovery returns the minimum needed to reach an agent, while catalog search, ranking and cost-based selection stay out of scope.
    That excluded part is what draft-artamokhov-dawn-marketplace-discovery addresses: how a requester finds catalogs (marketplaces) that list agents and tools across operators, through a well-known URI, before any selection happens.
    The two seem complementary: your model finds an entry point inside a managed network, and a catalog is used when the requester has to search beyond it.
    
    One question: should the metadata reference returned by bootstrap discovery be allowed to point to such a catalog, or do you see catalogs as entirely separate from bootstrap discovery?
    
    Best regards, Aleksandr Artamokhov
    
    01.11.2026, 05:47, Linda Dunbar <linda.dunbar=40futurewei.com@dmarc.ietf.org<mailto:linda.dunbar=40futurewei.com@dmarc.ietf.org>>
    Hi all,
    
    Thanks to Adrian for the detailed comments, and to everyone for the helpful discussion on the DAWN mailing list.
    
    We have updated draft https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-dunbar-dawn-infra-assisted-discovery/ . The revision aligns the terminology more closely with the DAWN terminology draft, in particular around MVD/MDI and the role of requester context. It also clarifies that the infrastructure-assisted model supports bootstrap discovery by contributing current resource state and requester context, without defining registration, catalog search, semantic matchmaking, ranking, or resource selection.
    
    The updated draft also distinguishes more clearly between DAWN bootstrap discovery and subsequent retrieval of richer agent-native metadata such as an A2A Agent Card.
    
    Comments and suggestions are very welcome.
    
    Best regards,
    Linda--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    Hi Siyu,
    
    One data point for your suggestion. The discovery document in draft-artamokhov-dawn-marketplace-discovery has no type field, and the clients that read it have not needed one. The well-known name already says the document describes a catalog, and each URL says its purpose by its member name: catalogue_url continues discovery, manifest_url is a description, mcp_endpoint is for interaction. So the condition could be "required unless the carrier or the Endpoint purpose already implies it".

## How this is computed

Adoption weighted by organic paying agents (wallets that also pay other services; captive/faucet wallets don't count), real depurated settlement, PageRank on the organic payment sub-graph (so fake wallets can't buy a rating), gated by uptime. The trust line is BBB. Outlook tracks the adoption trend week over week. A service is one entry regardless of how many networks it settles on. A listed resource that answers `410 Gone` with a `Sunset` date already past (RFC 8594) is a declared retirement: it leaves the uptime denominator instead of counting as down. A bare 410, a 404 or a 5xx counts as down.

Coverage: services listed in the x402 discovery catalogs (CDP Bazaar and PayAI), plus unlisted wallets seen settling on-chain; settlement measured in USDC on Base, Polygon, Arbitrum and Solana mainnets.

## Full ecosystem redeploy

Factory + Hub + Mesh + Alien Monitor — always from repo root, fixed order:
    
    `./scripts/deploy_ecosystem.sh
    `

Step  | Script
--- | ---
Factory  | `./scripts/deploy.sh`
Hub  | `./scripts/deploy_hub.sh`
Mesh  | `./scripts/deploy_mesh.sh`
Monitor  | `./scripts/deploy_alien_monitor.sh`
Verify  | `./scripts/verify_ecosystem_full.sh` (included in deploy_ecosystem unless `--skip-verify`)

Hub: do not redeploy with `cd aimarket-hub && docker compose up` — wrong build context; use `deploy_hub.sh` only. Details: `docs/deploy-ecosystem.md`.

## AIMarket Hub — modelmarket.dev (TLS)

Federation hub on `https://modelmarket.dev` (nginx `:443` → Docker hub `127.0.0.1:9083`).

Hub container (redeploy):
    
    `./scripts/deploy_hub.sh
    `

TLS bootstrap:
    
    `sudo [email protected] ./scripts/setup-modelmarket-ssl.sh
    `

Or: `docs/production-modelmarket-dev.md` — certbot + `certbot.timer` auto-renewal.

DNS: `modelmarket.dev` and `www` → same host as the factory.
